text: — Oh! Bay Ganyo, Christ is risen! Were you at the palace for the breaking of the fast?

— Who, me? Well, if it isn't me, who's it going to be? — Bay Ganyo answers me and, as he twirls his left mustache, he gives me a sly wink, meaning: “As long as there are fools in this world, would your Bay Ganyo miss out on the profit?”
— Well, how did it go? Was it fun?

— Who cares about being merry, there was plenty of loot to be had! I’d dressed myself up like... you know... You know, Holy Week, I fasted and fasted, bloating myself with those damned beans, and sauerkraut juice on top; I was as hungry as a bedbug. On Saturday, I didn’t put a crumb in my mouth. And then they went and set the breaking of the fast for two o’clock in the morning... While I stood in church, it felt as if three hundred leeches were sucking at my stomach. You spit and spit, and not a drop of saliva is left. You try to have a smoke—it doesn’t work, your mouth tastes bitter... They said "Christ is risen"—it was twelve o'clock, but how can you wait until two! I told my family to go and break the fast by themselves, and I went into "The Red Lobster." There, my brother, it was full of people like me—top hats, epaulettes, medals. And they were all waiting for two o'clock to strike. I sat down at a long table, and I saw a few bachelors breaking their fast. They had laid out that table with appetizers, suckling pigs, and Varna wine on top—enough to make your stomach weep. Just looking at the skin of the piglet, I nearly lost my mind. Well, what, I should have just asked those bachelors: "What are you eating there, eh! Pig? Bravo! Let me... you know... a little bit of the skin..."—and the people would have given me some. But no. I’ve been shy since I was a boy... (Give me your cigarette case, you smoke good tobacco; Ivanov’s is no good at all, smells like cheap mahorka...) Those bachelors started smacking their lips, it made me sick to watch them, so I turned my eyes away. I thought of spitting, but where was the spit! My guts were stuck together. I thought of ordering a beer, but then I changed my mind. Is that why I starved for, as they say, two days... I supposedly turned away so as not to look at them, but they, as if on purpose, damn them, kept chewing and kept praising the pig. I felt like, you know, getting up and snatching that damned pig right out of their mouths... If only I could bend over to press my stomach like that—you don't feel the hunger so much—but I couldn't bend over. My tailcoat is tight, it’ll split down the back. Oh, to hell with it! And the collar is starched so hard, it started scraping my neck like a saw... My eyes went dark. I left the Lobster and headed toward the palace. It’s not proper to go in early. I have a guard friend, a good friend too, even a bit of a relative if you ask me, but it still didn't feel right. And even if you go in early, it’s all the same, they won’t set a table for you right away. I circled and circled around the gates until my legs ached. Finally, at one point, *drrr*... a carriage, a little later *drrr*... another carriage. They entered the palace, thank God! I twirled my mustache a bit, cleared my throat, and off I went after them. I went inside, I saw the guards, the convoy, already lined up. A clean-shaven boy rushed to take off my coat, I muttered to him: "Excuse me, sir, mind your own business," and I didn't let him undress me. He got embarrassed and went to undress others. How could I let him undress me, brother? The sleeves of my coat—I mean not the sleeves, but the lining inside—was all torn up like... you know. Anyway. I went upstairs, but before I did, I cast an eye into the lower rooms—the tables were set, a clean job. A crowd gathered. We waited here a bit too, and then the Prince and Princess came out. This time, in a Christian way, they were the real host and hostess. They gave each of us an egg...
— Did you kiss a hand again?

— Well, naturally... Why, for a spread like that, I’d have kissed a hundred hands. Anyway. That ordeal passed too, and when we rushed down the stairs, my friend... Believe it or not, I was leaping over three steps at a time, I nearly crashed into the mirror, but I didn't let anyone get ahead of me. I got hold of the caviar, and when I dug in with the spoon—if it was less than half a kilo, let it be a sin on my soul. That fish mayonnaise, those appetizers, I don't even know their names, and when that mouth of mine gaped open... Forget it!... I ate and ate, I stuffed myself... and I still wonder how my stomach didn't burst. And the drinking... When I left, how I left—kill me, I don't remember... Ugh!... My head still aches from that damned champagne... And never mind that, but then I went and stuffed my pockets with pastries, and they were soft, devil take them, and they got all smeared inside my pocket... Well, goodbye then.
